transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-01-18
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 53 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Maya Chen, Rahul Patel (Redwood); Linda Park, Omar Reyes, Karen Li (AeroNova)

Summary:
Short demo focused on migration parity from OpenAI/Anthropic/Together -> Redwood API. Walked through API mapping, console parity (routes, model variants), and Optimize suggestions for batching/quantization. Customer raised VPC/networking and SSO/enterprise compliance concerns. Agreed to share parity spreadsheet and run a small pilot with sample traffic.

Topics:
- API call mapping (parameters, tokenization diffs)
- Model behavior parity and output tuning
- Console: routing, model variants, rollouts and tracing
- Redwood Optimize: batching, KV cache, quantization profile recommendations
- Deployment modes: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC) and tradeoffs
- Security: SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs, SSO/SAML

Transcript body:
[00:00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Maya, AE at Redwood, and Rahul Patel our solutions engineer is with me. How's the audio?
[00:00:08] Linda Park: Hi Maya, good thanks. Can you hear me?
[00:00:10] Rahul Patel: Yep loud and clear. Thanks Linda. Omar, Karen, you there?
[00:00:13] Omar Reyes: Yep, here. Sorry we had to shuffle some folks.
[00:00:16] Karen Li: All good. We have about 50 minutes, right?
[00:00:18] Maya Chen: Yup, roughly. We'll try to keep to the parity demo and leave time for questions and next steps. Quick agenda — api mapping, console tour, optimize tips, then Q&A.
[00:00:28] Omar Reyes: Sounds great. Our main asks: 1) low effort swap for our OpenAI endpoints, 2) cost and latency comparatives, and 3) enterprise security fit.
[00:00:37] Maya Chen: Perfect. Rahul — want to kick off with the API mapping?
[00:00:40] Rahul Patel: Sure. So first, the good news — Redwood's REST surface mirrors common patterns: messages/inputs, temperature, max_tokens, top_p, stop sequences. For Together and Anthropic you'll see slightly different param names, e.g., Together's "ctx" or Anthropic's "max_tokens_to_sample" — we normalise those.
[00:01:03] Linda Park: When you say normalise, do you do runtime translation or do we have to update our client code?
[00:01:08] Rahul Patel: Both options. We provide a drop-in shim snippet that maps the few vendor-specific fields to Redwood's fields so your clients can stay the same. Alternatively, you can change a single config switch in the SDK to point to Redwood and we handle the rest server-side.
[00:01:21] Karen Li: Are there any tokenization mismatches we should be worried about? We saw some differences moving from model X to Y before.
[00:01:26] Rahul Patel: Good call. Tokenization can cause slight token-count variances. Redwood exposes tokenizers for major models and we include a pre-flight token counter in the SDK so you can reconcile billing and truncate safely. For Anthropic style prompts you might see +/- 1-3 tokens depending on the model length.
[00:01:44] Omar Reyes: Ok, and how about streaming? Our realtime chat uses streaming extensively.
[00:01:48] Maya Chen: We support streaming with chunked responses and have a small demo later. Note: for very short latencies we recommend pairing streaming with our lightweight KV cache to avoid recompute on repeated prefixes. Rahul will show that.
[00:01:59] Rahul Patel: Jump to the console — I'm sharing screen. (brief pause, screen switch)
[00:02:12] Rahul Patel: Here is the Models tab. You'll notice we label variants and put a compatibility badge for OpenAI/Anthropic/Together drop-in parity. You can pin a variant per-route or setup a fallback chain — so if a high-perf variant is OOM or throttled, we fall back to a cheaper subset automatically.
[00:02:33] Linda Park: That fallback thing — is that per-request or per-route?
[00:02:36] Rahul Patel: Per-route policy with per-request override. So most customers set route level SLOs and the runtime will choose the best model variant to meet latency/cost SLOs.
[00:02:46] Karen Li: Anything special for Dedicated or Private? Our security team will push for VPC peering or even on-prem in the future.
[00:02:52] Maya Chen: Yes — Dedicated gives you reserved capacity with guaranteed throughput and private deployments (VPC or on-prem) get the control plane in your network. For VPC we do peering with encrypted traffic and support customer KMS/HSM integration for keys.
[00:03:05] Omar Reyes: Do audit logs include token-level redaction? We can't store raw data in logs.
[00:03:09] Maya Chen: Good question — we support both redacted audit logs and full audit logs depending on your compliance level; for enterprise pilots we commonly enable redaction and forward hashed token fingerprints for debugging. We'll share the security page.
[00:03:21] Rahul Patel: Back to parity — here's a sample request mapping from OpenAI's chat completions to Redwood. (reads snippet) Replace model param with our model alias, move 'stop' unchanged, and set streaming=true. The token cost per-call will be slightly different if the tokenizer differs; we show estimated tokens and cost in the Console during tests.
[00:03:42] Linda Park: Any differences in hallucination behavior across models? We've used Anthropic for safety reasons.
[00:03:47] Rahul Patel: Behavioral parity is tricky — we pair model selection with small prompt transformations and safety filters. For Anthropic-style safety we recommend their calibrated prompts, and Redwood Optimize can run guardrails that rerank or rerun a smaller safety-model check. It's not a magic bullet but it reduces regression risk.
[00:04:06] Omar Reyes: Can Optimize do automated batching suggestions per-route?
[00:04:10] Rahul Patel: Yes, Optimize analyzes your traffic patterns and suggests batch sizes, TTLs for the KV cache, and quantization profiles. For example, if you have lots of short chats, Optimize may recommend aggressive prefix caching and a 4-bit quant model on CPU fallback to save costs.
[00:04:24] Karen Li: How does KV cache interact with privacy? Is cached content ever written to logs?
[00:04:28] Maya Chen: Cache is in-memory by default and we can configure it to be ephemeral per-request or persistent depending on policy. We treat KV cache as data in scope for encryption and can hook it to your KMS.
[00:04:39] Linda Park: Can we see a quick latency comparison? We're sensitive to 95th percentile.
[00:04:44] Rahul Patel: I prepared a small run using a sample trace you provided earlier — will run a tiny playback. (runs demo) So baseline, OpenAI's 95th was ~230ms on similar infra in our tests, Redwood hosted variant here shows 210ms, dedicated GPU pool shows 95th around 120ms for the model we selected. Note these are synthetic and we'll need your real traces to be precise.
[00:05:15] Omar Reyes: Wait you said 120ms — what's the sequence length and batch size?
[00:05:18] Rahul Patel: Right — that was for an average 64-token response with batching at 8 and KV cache hits at ~15% so less decode. We'll share the runbook and the script.
[00:05:29] Karen Li: If we go dedicated, what's the contractual cadence and commitment?
[00:05:33] Maya Chen: Dedicated is reserved capacity with monthly or annual commits; we typically do a 3-month pilot on a small commit and then scale. Pricing varies by GPU type and region — we'll send a tailored pricing sheet.
[00:05:44] Linda Park: Our security team will want SOC2 evidence and SAML SSO for team access.
[00:05:48] Maya Chen: We have SOC2 Type II and support SAML/SSO, RBAC, and audit log exports to your SIEM. I'll attach the security pack.
[00:05:56] Omar Reyes: For model rollouts, can we run canaries and A/B with traffic splitting?
[00:06:00] Rahul Patel: Yeah — the Console supports canary rollouts and per-route traffic split. You can also configure automatic fallback thresholds if latency or error rate spikes.
[00:06:09] Karen Li: Any gotchas moving from Together? We use some Together-only params like 'context_window' and some custom sampling.
[00:06:16] Rahul Patel: We mapped Together's context_window to our limit mapping and expose runtime warnings if you exceed a model's context. For sampling, we preserve temperature/top_p semantics and expose a compatibility layer for their extra knobs. There may be minor tuning needed for deterministic outputs.
[00:06:33] Linda Park: Ok, quick question about token billing — if tokens differ due to tokenizer, will Redwood bill differently?
[00:06:39] Maya Chen: We bill on our token counts; but during migration we provide a reconciliation period where we show both OpenAI/Anthropic token estimates side-by-side so you can project costs.
[00:06:49] Omar Reyes: Great. Anything for latency SLO enforcement? We want circuit breakers if an endpoint breaches 95th for more than 2 minutes.
[00:06:55] Rahul Patel: You can set route-level SLOs and policies for circuit-breaker thresholds; the runtime will automatically reroute to fallback variants, and we emit traces and alerts to the console + webhook to your pager.
[00:07:07] Karen Li: Could you show the Optimize suggestions tab?
[00:07:10] Rahul Patel: Sure — Optimize shows candidate changes with estimated cost delta and perf impact. Here's a sample: enable prefix caching for route '/chat', set batch_size 12, and apply 4-bit quant for CPU fallback. Estimated cost reduction 35% with 5-10% increase in average latency on fallback only.
[00:07:29] Linda Park: Hmm, 35% is attractive. What's the quality hit with 4-bit quant? We do doc summarization so quality matters.
[00:07:34] Rahul Patel: For summarization we often recommend mixed strategy: use high-precision variants for the initial generation and fallback to quantized models only for non-critical requests or lower-fidelity modes. We can run an eval set against your prompts to quantify ROUGE/accuracy changes.
[00:07:49] Omar Reyes: We'll definitely run an eval. Can Redwood host the eval or do we run it?
[00:07:53] Maya Chen: We can help run it as part of the pilot, or hand you the eval harness. Many customers prefer the joint run so we can tune recommendations.
[00:07:59] Karen Li: Back to networking: do you support private link / AWS VPC endpoints to avoid internet egress?
[00:08:05] Rahul Patel: Yes, we support VPC endpoints for major clouds and private link style peering. We'll need your networking CIDR and egress policy to propose the setup.
[00:08:14] Linda Park: Anything else we should be aware of?
[00:08:17] Maya Chen: One more operational note: we expose per-token and per-route cost breakdowns and trace links so you can drill into slow requests. That often helps engineering prioritize prompt or model changes.
[00:08:28] Omar Reyes: Great. Let's open the next steps and timeline.
[00:08:32] Maya Chen: Proposed: share parity spreadsheet and console clip by Thursday; AeroNova share traffic traces and constraints by next Friday; pilot kickoff the following Monday. Rahul will prepare a latency demo with your traces.
[00:08:45] Karen Li: Works for us. Also we'll need the security artifacts before we present to procurement.
[00:08:50] Maya Chen: Absolutely. We'll add SOC2 + KMS notes and a draft contract template in the package.
[00:08:57] Linda Park: Thanks everyone. A few quick clarifying questions from Omar — will Optimize suggestions be auto-applied or advisory?
[00:09:04] Rahul Patel: Advisory by default. You can opt into auto-apply for non-critical routes, but it requires admin approval.
[00:09:12] Omar Reyes: Makes sense.
[00:09:14] Maya Chen: Alright we'll wrap. Rahul, any final notes?
[00:09:17] Rahul Patel: Just that we try to make the migration low-friction: shim code, one-config SDK, and console tools for parity testing. Expect the parity spreadsheet to include per-endpoint mapping, sample payloads, and expected token deltas.
[00:09:31] Linda Park: Perfect. Thanks.
[00:09:34] Karen Li: Thanks all.
[00:09:36] Maya Chen: Thanks AeroNova team. We'll follow up with materials and schedule the pilot kickoff.

(End of captured transcript — remaining meeting time included Q&A and small side-discussion about procurement calendar, some crosstalk that the recorder garbled.)
